documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up and endoscopy with banding (visit 2024-12-31)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 12/31/2024

Mr. Pomeroy is a 54-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis and esophageal varices, here for his scheduled yearly visit and repeat endoscopy. About a week ago he brought up blood once; he thought it was from his old ulcer. Nothing since: no further vomiting, no change in his stools, no belly pain. He acknowledges ongoing drinking this fall; his most recent drink was two days ago. Hospitalized in September for encephalopathy.

Meds: propranolol 20 mg BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, spironolactone 100 mg, furosemide 40 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg.
Allergies: none.

Exam: Vitals stable. Alert, no asterixis. Spleen mildly enlarged to palpation. No ascites detected. No caput medusae.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, platelets 90, INR 1.2, AST 70, ALT 30, alkaline phosphatase 100, albumin 3.2.

Procedure: EGD under monitored anesthesia care. Large varices in the lower third of the esophagus without active bleeding. Band ligation performed; four bands placed. No gastric varices. No ulcer in the stomach or duodenum.

Impression: Varices have progressed from small to large despite propranolol; the recent single episode of hematemesis is presumed variceal in origin.

Plan:
1. Continue propranolol 20 mg BID.
2. Repeat banding in about 4 weeks and then at intervals until the varices are eradicated.
3. Continue lactulose and diuretics.
4. Abstinence strongly advised; he is re-engaging with treatment.
5. Any further bleeding: emergency department immediately.

Gastroenterology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No liver mass. Small amount of fluid, known. Next surveillance in July. Will discuss at Feb visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u. Missed November. GI letter for 12/31 received mid-January: varices now large, banded, one episode of vomiting blood the week before. He tells me he had the second banding on 1/28 - no paperwork from that one; throat sore for two days, otherwise fine.

Alcohol: cut way down since the new year but "a few on Saturdays." Back at the program one evening a week. AUDIT-C 6. Wife says no confusion; lactulose 2-3 BMs/day.
No further hematemesis, no black stools.

Exam: BP 118/74, HR 62. Wt 79. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, mild flank dullness. Spider angiomas. No edema. No asterixis.

US 1/21: no lesion, small ascites.

A/P
1. Large esophageal varices, banding series underway with GI; propranolol continues; HR fine.
2. Cirrhosis with small ascites - diuretics same; BMP today.
3. HE on lactulose - no recurrence.
4. AUD - still drinking on weekends. Asked him to tell his GI team the same. We talked about the next bleed being the dangerous one.
5. Lung screening CT: he still does not want it this year. Order closed; will revisit in the fall.

RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: He was in the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Linda writing for Scott. He was in the hospital again from Tuesday to Saturday last week. Same thing as September, he got very confused and his stomach blew up. They drained a lot of fluid out. He is home and clearer now. They said to follow up with you. Can we get an appointment? Also they gave him new papers but nothing about his meds changed.

documents.title: RE: He was in the hospital again
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you for letting us know, Linda. I booked him for Tuesday 4/22 at 1:40 with the doctor. Please bring the discharge papers. We have asked the hospital to fax the summary. If he gets confused again, has a fever, belly pain, or any blood in vomit or stool, go straight to the emergency room.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit; discharge summary not yet received - working from the patient's papers and wife's account.

Admitted 4/8-4/12: confusion again with a tense belly; large-volume paracentesis; lactulose continued. Papers list the same medications as before.

Today: clear-headed, oriented. Admits the lactulose had slipped to once a day before the admission because it was inconvenient when out on errands. Back to twice daily now, 2-3 BMs. Drinking: admits weekend beers through March. Says he is done; skeptical look from his wife.

Exam: BP 116/72. Wt 77. Anicteric. Abdomen moderately soft, small amount of flank dullness, paracentesis site healed. No asterixis. No edema.

A/P
1. Recurrent hepatic encephalopathy - second admission. Lactulose BID, titrate to 2-3 BMs, not fewer. Wife to keep the BM count on the fridge.
2. Recurrent ascites - post-paracentesis; diuretics same, low salt.
3. Large varices - next banding per GI.
4. AUD - ongoing use; he says he wants to go back to more intensive sessions. Encouraged him to call the program this week.
5. Labs today. Request discharge summary again.

RTC 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-hospital labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs yesterday: bilirubin 2.6, albumin 3.0, INR 1.4, platelets 84, hemoglobin 11.6, sodium 132. These are the weakest numbers your liver has shown, Scott. Kidneys are fine. This is the point where stopping drinking for good changes what happens next. No medication changes.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (admitted 2025-04-08, discharged 2025-04-12)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/08/2025  Discharged 04/12/2025

Diagnoses: Hepatic encephalopathy, recurrent. Tense ascites in alcohol-related cirrhosis. Esophageal varices, under banding. Alcohol use disorder.

Presentation: Brought in by wife for two days of confusion and sleepiness with a tight abdomen. Encephalopathic on arrival with asterixis. Tense ascites.

Course: Large-volume paracentesis on day 1 with albumin replacement; fluid without evidence of infection. Lactulose increased in hospital with clearing of mentation by day 3; home dosing resumed at discharge. No bleeding. Patient reported intermittent alcohol use; counseled.

Discharge medications (unchanged): lactulose 30 mL BID, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, propranolol 20 mg BID, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks; GI for continued banding.

documents.title: No-show outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Missed 10:20 appt. Called home and cell, left message on cell asking him to call back to reschedule and to confirm he is ok. Will try wife's number tomorrow if no call back.

documents.title: No-show outreach, follow-up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reached wife. He is home, not confused, taking his meds; overslept yesterday. Rebooked for August after his next ultrasound. She will call sooner if anything changes.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doc. Wanted you to know I went back to the program full time the first week of July, 3 nights a week. Last beer was June 24. I'm doing it for real this time. See you in August.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Scott, this is the best message I have had all month. Thank you for telling me. Keep going to every session. See you in August - and call any time before then.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u cirrhosis. Seven weeks sober (last drink 6/24), program three nights a week, has a sponsor. Looks better than April - color, energy. No confusion, lactulose 2-3 BMs. No bleeding. Belly flat. Banding sessions with GI he says are spaced out over the summer; no letters from them since January.

Meds: propranolol 20 BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, pantoprazole 40, amlodipine 5.

Exam: BP 118/74, HR 64. Wt 76. Anicteric. Spider angiomas. Abdomen soft, no shifting dullness. No asterixis. No edema.

US 8/5: no mass, no ascites.

A/P
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis - improving with abstinence. Labs today.
2. AUD - early remission again, engaged.
3. Varices - banding with GI; asked him to sign a release so GI sends procedure notes.
4. HE - none since April.
5. Physical in November; flu/COVID in October.

RTC November.

documents.title: August labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good direction: bilirubin 1.9 (from 2.6 in April), albumin 3.3, sodium back to normal, liver enzymes lower. Platelets 88 - stable for you. Seven weeks of sobriety already shows. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid and 2025-26 COVID vaccine R deltoid. Last year's flu shot was declined; no reaction history. Observed 15 min. Pt says 3 months sober this week.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM

55 y/o man. Sober since late June, four months now; still going to his program and meets his sponsor weekly. No cigarettes since 2023. Living at home with his wife; on disability.

No confusion episodes since April. No hematemesis or melena. A little more tired than he would like. Belly stable.

Meds: propranolol 20 BID, lactulose 30 mL BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, pantoprazole 40, amlodipine 5. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Alert, oriented. Sclerae clear. Mouth and throat normal. Neck without nodes. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended, spleen tip palpable. Spider angiomas upper chest. Palmar erythema. No edema. No asterixis. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-9 2, AUDIT-C 0.

A/P
- Alcoholic cirrhosis, portal hypertension, large varices with banding, HE and ascites history: stable on current regimen. Labs today.
- Prevention: flu and COVID done 10/7; Tdap 2021; PCV20 2021; Shingrix complete; hep A/B complete. Colon screening: FIT last done 2023 - kit given today. Lung CT due; he agrees this year - ordered.
- AUD in early remission.

RTC 3 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Indication: Former smoker, approximately 20 pack-years, quit 2023.
Comparison: 11/14/2023.
Findings: No lung nodules. No consolidation. No emphysema. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. No lymphadenopathy. Upper abdomen: cirrhotic liver contour and splenomegaly, previously characterized.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung CT negative again, Lung-RADS 1. Next in a year.

documents.title: Wife calling - ED visit, vomiting blood
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. Yesterday afternoon he threw up a large amount of blood at home; she drove him to the ED. They gave fluids, did a scope, and banded "a vein that had bled". He is admitted, stable this morning, talking normally. She says he had been more tired for a few weeks and full quickly at meals. He has not been drinking since late June. Asked her to have the hospital send records; gave fax. Booked post-discharge visit 1/8 if he is out by then. Routed to PCP urgent FYI.
